title: Methods for next generation three-dimensional histology for human neural tissues
protocol: Immerse whole or hemi-sected human brain tissue in 10% neutral buffered formalin solution for 3-4 weeks, suspending it using an inverted porous disposable hairnet to minimize fixation artifacts.
Alternatively, cut brain tissue into 1 cm³ cubes and immerse them into 10% neutral buffered formalin solution for 7 days.
Melt away excess paraffin wax at 60°C in an incubation oven.
Retrieve tissue from the molten paraffin wax and put it into a screw-capped glass bottle with xylene, incubate at 55 – 60°C for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Immerse the tissue into 100% tetrahydrofuran (THF) in a screw-capped glass bottle to elute all the xylene out and ensure complete deparaffinisation, incubate for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Immerse the tissue into 80% THF in water in a screw-capped glass bottle for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Immerse the tissue into 50% THF in water in a screw-capped glass bottle for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Immerse the tissue into 20% THF in water in a screw-capped glass bottle for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Immerse the tissue into SBC solution.
Incubate at 55°C.
Proceed to the usual 3D histology protocol starting from the SDS treatment step.
If the tissue is deemed not well-fixed, immerse in neutral buffered formalin.
Incubate for an additional 3 days at room temperature or overnight at 37ºC.
Cut the tissue to the desired size using a razor blade, microtome blade, or disposable scalpel.
Immerse tissue into SBC solution.
Incubate at 37-55°C.
Incubate tissue in SDS solution for up to three months, as time allows.
Immerse tissue in formalin for an additional 3 days at room temperature or overnight at 37°C if fixed for less than a week.
Wash the tissue in PBST at 37°C for 2 hours; repeat this step three times.
Use a plastic pipette to carefully extract all solution around the tissue and apply new solution using a clean pipette.
Incubate tissue with primary antibody diluted in PBST at 37°C, starting with a low concentration such as 1:500 to 1:100 dilution.
Supplement antibody over the next 1 – 2 days to achieve the desired final dilution of 1:20 to 1:50.
Wash the tissue in PBST at 37°C for 3 x 2 hours and leave overnight.
Incubate the tissue with secondary antibody diluted in PBST at 37°C, protecting from light using aluminum foil.
Wash the tissue in PBST at 37°C for 3 x 2 hours and leave overnight.
Remove the tissue from the washing solution.
Blot off excess washing solution from the tissue gently using Kimwipe paper.
Place the tissue into OPTIClear solution, incubate at 37°C for about 6 hours to clear the tissue.
Incubate tissue until complete transparency is reached within 3 hours.
Swirl contents gently and occasionally if necessary to facilitate reagent penetration into the tissue.
Store tissue in OPTIClear at room temperature protected from light before imaging (up to 1 week).
For prolonged storage, place tissue in PBS at 4°C.
Add 0.01% sodium azide to PBS for prolonged storage to avoid microbial growth.
Carefully place tissue into a glass-bottomed imaging dish for confocal imaging.
Tip the cleared tissue from its container directly into the imaging dish.
Use a clean pipette to carefully extract excess OPTIClear solution around the tissue.
Allow tissue to adhere to the bottom of the imaging dish once all surrounding solution has been extracted.
Blot off any excess solution carefully using Kimwipe paper around the tissue.
Apply a few drops of OPTIClear on the tissue just before imaging to prevent drying during prolonged imaging.
Cover the imaging dish with a lid before proceeding to confocal imaging.
Incubate the tissue in Nissl staining solution for 1 – 3 hours at room temperature.
Place the tissue into regression solution at room temperature to regress the staining.
Swirl and refresh the regression solution until no observable violet tint is coming out of the tissue.
Do not prolong the regression process for more than 30 minutes.
If the tissue is thick and large (> 5 mm-thick, or > 2 cm x 2 cm in height and width), perform serial dehydration through dilutions of regression solution in water.
Proceed to 3D immunohistochemistry.
Wash in PBST for 6 hours at 37°C.
Place the tissue into OPTIClear and incubate for 3 hours to overnight at 60°C.
Store the tissue in OPTIClear at room temperature protected from light before imaging (up to 1 week).
For prolonged storage, place the tissue in PBS at 4°C with 0.01% sodium azide added.
Image the tissue with a 488 nm Argon laser excitation.
Adjust the detection spectra range accordingly to obtain good contrast and avoid autofluorescence.
Use a range of 570 – 700 nm as an empirical start range.
Place a crystal or powder of lipophilic dye on the brain tissue.
Poke the crystal deep below the tissue surface with a needle.
Soak the tissue in 1x PBS to keep it moist.
Cover and seal the plate carefully without disturbing the system inside.
Incubate the setup at 37°C free from any disturbances for a variable period of time.
Blot off excess liquid on the tissue after tracing is deemed sufficient.
Place the tissue in OPTIClear for clearing for 6 – 15 hours at 37°C.
Store the tissue in OPTIClear at room temperature protected from light before imaging.
For prolonged storage, place the tissue in PBS at 4°C and add 0.01% sodium azide to avoid microbial growth.
Proceed to confocal imaging.
